answer: A print shop gives each agent one copper plate engraved with a fable of its own. Each epoch the agent etches one fresh line into the plate, pulls one print, and signs the margin with a plume dipped in iron ink. A binder files the print against the plate and the signature, and only a plate whose etching, print, and signature all match earns a stamp in the registry. A thousand fake names need a thousand copper plates engraved line by line, a thousand prints pulled, and a thousand plume signatures that pass the binder, so copying one plate buys nothing.
